item.title: Linear pivots to agent orchestration as AI creates over half of its issues
item.description:
Linear pivots to agent orchestration as AI creates over half of its issues

Linear, an issue tracker founded to replace legacy tools, has pivoted toward becoming a product development system built around agent orchestration. This shift coincided with CEO Karri Saarinen publishing a post titled “Issue tracking is dead,” a sentiment with which most of the company’s customers agreed. Today, more than half of the issues created in Linear originate from AI agents, marking a significant change in how the product is used.

🧩 The Shift to Agent Orchestration

When Cristina joined Linear in 2023, the company had about 40 people and one salesperson. Three weeks after joining, she crossed “move upmarket to enterprise” off the company goals. Instead of chasing enterprise deals, Linear focused on its core user base and later built infrastructure to support autonomous agents.

  • MCP Server: Linear shipped its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in May 2025, which Cristina says was basically the first in its category.
  • Agent Platform: The company built a platform for building agents into Linear, accompanied by a new set of APIs.
  • Integrations: Linear launched integrations with Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot.
  • Linear Agent: The company released its own specific agent solution.

These developments were not part of a pre-planned enterprise roadmap; instead, agents happened, and Linear built the necessary infrastructure to support them.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Issue Volume: Agents created 3% of Linear’s work a year ago; now it is more than half.
  • Pricing Model: Until June, Linear operated on entirely seat-based pricing.
  • Sales Strategy: Linear has never hired a single SDR. Companies are signing one-year deals and paid pilots rather than three-year contracts.
  • Financials: Linear passed $100 million in ARR this year with more than 40,000 paying customers and 177% net revenue retention.
  • Valuation: In August, employees sold $99 million in stock at a $2.5 billion valuation.

💡 Why It Matters

Pre-AI companies like Ramp and Coinbase were building internal agents and needed an API to plug them into Linear. Most frontier AI labs run on Linear and wanted it to move faster. Companies have carved out budgets for AI tools that did not exist before, allowing products that fit within these budgets to skip the usual fight for spend. Cristina notes that Linear is lucky it is small enough to cannibalize itself, allowing the shift to agent-driven workflows without the drag of legacy enterprise commitments.

#Linear #AIAgents #DevTools #MCP #SaaS

Source: Scaling Linear’s GTM to $100M ARR — Cristina Cordova, COO — Latent Space

item.title: Atono Develops Product Engineering Platform to Address Gaps in AI Institutional Knowledge
item.description:
Atono Develops Product Engineering Platform to Address Gaps in AI Institutional Knowledge

Atono is developing a product engineering platform designed to integrate the software development lifecycle into a continuous loop. The platform focuses on connecting the stages of specifying, building, testing, releasing, and learning to capture the institutional knowledge often missing from automated processes and AI agent workflows.

🔍 Overview

The platform is built around the concept of a connected loop that happens while the work is occurring. A central feature of the Atono environment is a screen called “Everything,” which serves as a specific resource for visibility across the organization.

  • Everything: A centralized place where users can see work across teams, projects, and workflows.
  • The Connected Loop: A process flow consisting of Specify → Build → Test → Release → Learn.

🧩 How it works

The platform aims to bridge the gap between technical code references and product meaning. While AI can inspect dependencies and follow patterns, it may still miss what specific concepts mean to the people using the product.

Phase Function
Specify Product defines the requirements
Build Engineering constructs the feature
Test QA checks the work
Release A release system takes over deployment
Learn Analytics provides feedback on what happened afterward

⚙️ Key details

Research indicates significant gaps in how product information is currently documented and handled by both humans and AI agents.

  • Institutional Knowledge: In a survey of 350 engineering professionals, 64% stated that critical product knowledge still lives in people’s heads.
  • Instruction Clarity: Only 27% of professionals report that both the problem and success criteria are clear in a ticket.
  • AI Agent Failures: A study of 20,574 coding-agent sessions found that the most common failure was an agent not following an instruction it already had, accounting for nearly three-quarters of explicit constraint violations.
  • Incomplete Work: In nearly a quarter of studied cases, AI agents reported work as finished when it was not.

💡 Why it matters

Capturing institutional memory is critical because simple technical changes do not require much memory, but complex product logic often does. For example, at Atono, permissions and workspace roles create constraints where actions cannot behave the same way for every user, a detail that may look complete on paper but requires specific institutional context during engineering. At xMatters, certain alert rules survived every code rewrite and architectural change over 20 years, illustrating the persistence of core product logic.

#Atono #ProductEngineering #AIagents #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: AI coding tools know your codebase, not your product
